fields.effective: From when do you pay the new rent?
fields.current_rent: Your current net cold rent (per month)
fields.agreed_rent: Net cold rent you consent to (per month)
fields.disputed_plus: The landlord’s plus features that you do not accept
fields.missing_minus: Minus features the landlord has not taken into account
fields.tenant_name_help: As it is written in the tenancy agreement. If several people signed the agreement, all of them should sign.
fields.received_help: This is important for all deadlines. Write down the date and keep the envelope.
fields.contract_number_help: Often at the top of the landlord’s letter.
fields.agreed_rent_help: Only enter an amount you are sure is correct. You are bound by it.
fields.effective_help: Enter the date from the landlord’s letter. If this date is earlier than the start of the third calendar month after receipt, the later day applies. The calculator fills the field with the later of the two days. Check it.
fields.disputed_plus_help: Only choose features that you have checked yourself.
fields.missing_minus_help: Only choose features that you have checked in your flat and can prove.
fields.own_text_help: We do not check this text. It goes into the letter unchanged. Only write facts that are true. Do not put conditions or a counter-offer („nur wenn …“, “only if …”) into a consent. Then the consent can count as a refusal.
fields.current_rent_help: Without service charges and heating costs.

intro.title: Letter to the landlord
intro.text: The letter is in German because your landlord must understand it. The explanations here are in your language. Read the letter carefully before you send it. We do not check your case.

send.title: How to send the letter
send.text: Sign the letter. Send it in a way that lets you show later that it arrived: for example by registered mail with proof of delivery (Einwurf-Einschreiben), or hand it in together with a witness. Keep a copy. The letter must arrive before your deadline ends.

mietspiegel_choice.title: Which Mietspiegel applies?
mietspiegel_choice.text: What counts is the day the rent increase demand (Mieterhöhungsverlangen) reaches you (receipt, Zugang). The local comparative rent is determined for this day (BGH, VIII ZR 22/20, Rn. 29). Usually the Mietspiegel that applies on that day is used: from 28.05.2026 the Mietspiegel 2026, from 30.05.2024 to 27.05.2026 the Mietspiegel 2024. Note: if the letter arrived between 01.09.2025 and 27.05.2026, a court may also use the Mietspiegel 2026 or add a surcharge (LG Berlin, 65 S 527/13; BGH, VIII ZR 295/15). In that case, calculate with both. For the rent brake (Mietpreisbremse), on the other hand, what matters is the start of the tenancy.

ovm.title: Local comparative rent (ortsübliche Vergleichsmiete)
ovm.text: This is the rent that is usual in Berlin for similar flats (§ 558 Abs. 2 BGB). The calculator takes the value from your Mietspiegel field and places it in the range with the Orientierungshilfe. The result is an estimate based on your details. The new rent must not be higher than this value.

netting.title: How the range is applied
netting.text: In each of the five groups, you count plus and minus features. More plus: the group counts as plus. More minus: as minus. Equal: 0. Then you weigh the groups against each other: one plus group and one minus group cancel each other out. Each plus moves the value up by one fifth of the distance from the average value to the upper value, each minus moves it down by one fifth of the distance to the lower value (Mietspiegel No. 10.3). The Mietspiegel does not say whether to round per group or once. Differences of one cent are possible.

consent_deadline.title: Your deadline for consent
consent_deadline.text: You have time until the end of the second calendar month after the month in which the letter arrived (§ 558b Abs. 2 BGB). Your reply should reach the landlord by this day. If the day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Berlin, the wording of § 193 BGB moves the end to the next working day. We have not found a court decision on exactly this point. So do not rely on this.

effective.title: From when the new rent applies
effective.text: If you consent, you pay the higher rent from the start of the third calendar month after receipt (§ 558b Abs. 1 BGB). If the landlord names a later date, the later date applies. If on that date the rent has not yet been unchanged for 15 months, the increase can apply at the earliest when the 15 months are over (§ 558 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB).

sue_deadline.title: Deadline for the landlord to sue
sue_deadline.text: If you do not consent, or only consent in part, the landlord can sue for consent. The court case must be filed within three months after the end of your deadline (§ 558b Abs. 2 BGB). If the end falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Berlin, the landlord has until the next working day, for example until Monday (§ 193 BGB). It is enough if the claim reaches the court by then and is served soon afterwards (§ 167 ZPO). That is why we show the later date here. After that, the landlord can no longer sue for this increase; a new demand is still possible.

termination_declare_by.title: Special termination: deadline (common interpretation)
termination_declare_by.text: After a rent increase demand you can terminate the tenancy with extraordinary notice, until the end of the second month after receipt (§ 561 BGB). The date shown here is the end of the second calendar month. We have not found this reading confirmed in an official source. It is better to use the safe date. Here too, we do not move the date to a working day.

termination_safe_by.title: Special termination: safe date
termination_safe_by.text: If your notice of termination reaches the landlord by this day (two months from receipt), you are on the safe side (§ 561 BGB). This also applies if the day is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday: it is not settled whether the deadline then moves. Do not count on it. The notice must be in writing, on paper with your signature (§ 568 Abs. 1 BGB). The rent increase then does not apply.

termination_ends.title: End of the tenancy after special termination
termination_ends.text: The tenancy ends at the end of the second month after the month in which your notice arrives (§ 561 Abs. 1 BGB). The date shown applies if the notice arrives on the last possible day. If you give notice earlier, it ends earlier.

sperrfrist_earliest_received.title: One-year blocking period (Sperrfrist)
sperrfrist_earliest_received.text: A rent increase demand may reach you one year after the last rent increase at the earliest (§ 558 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB). The year counts from the day the last increase took effect (BGH, VIII ZR 141/09, Rn. 18). If it arrives earlier, it is invalid (BGH, VIII ZR 178/03). Increases after a modernisation or for service charges (§§ 559 to 560 BGB) do not count.

wartefrist_earliest_effective.title: 15-month waiting period (Wartefrist)
wartefrist_earliest_effective.text: The new rent may only apply when the rent has been unchanged for 15 months (§ 558 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB). The 15 months count from the date the last increase was first due (BGH, VIII ZR 178/03). Increases for modernisation or service charges do not count.

kappung.title: Cap of 15 % (Kappungsgrenze)
kappung.text: In Berlin, increases under § 558 BGB may raise the rent by at most 15 % within three years (§ 558 Abs. 3 BGB, Berliner Kappungsgrenzenverordnung of 14.03.2023, valid until 10.05.2028). The starting point is the rent three years before the day the new rent is to apply (BGH, VIII ZR 177/03). Increases of the cold rent after a modernisation (§ 559 BGB) do not count towards the 15 %: the 15 % is calculated without them, and such an increase may come on top. Changes to the advance payments for service charges are not part of it.

silence.title: Silence is not consent
silence.text: If you do nothing, you have not consented. The landlord can then sue (§ 558b Abs. 2 BGB).

payment_consent.title: Paying can be consent
payment_consent.text: Consent does not need any particular form. If you pay the higher rent several times without reservation, this can count as consent (BGH, VIII ZB 74/16, Rn. 13, 21).

consent_binding.title: Consent is final
consent_binding.text: You can no longer take back a consent, including a partial one, once it has reached the landlord (§ 130 Abs. 1 BGB). A withdrawal like with an online purchase is not possible either (BGH, VIII ZR 94/17; VIII ZR 62/18, Rn. 21 f.). The rent then counts as agreed. Only in exceptional cases, for example deliberate deception, can you challenge it (anfechten, § 123 BGB). As a rule, you can no longer rely on the rent brake (Mietpreisbremse) against the new rent (BGH, VIII ZR 300/21).

partial_consent.title: Partial consent
partial_consent.text: You can also consent to only part of the increase (§ 558b Abs. 1 BGB: „soweit“, “to the extent that”). You are bound by it. The landlord can sue for the rest (BGH, VIII ZR 141/09, Rn. 19). Afterwards, pay only the amount you consented to.

landlord_equipment.title: Only the landlord’s fittings count
landlord_equipment.text: What you installed and paid for yourself does not count (Mietspiegel 2026 No. 6.3), and this is permanent (BGH, VIII ZR 52/18). It is different if the landlord paid you back the costs. For the area, the real living space counts, not the number in the tenancy agreement (BGH, VIII ZR 266/14).

burden_of_proof.title: Who has to prove what?
burden_of_proof.text: In a court case, the landlord has to prove the local comparative rent (BGH, VIII ZR 123/20, Rn. 27). On the individual features, the Landgericht Berlin (Berlin Regional Court, today Landgericht Berlin II) decided: the landlord has to prove plus features; you have to prove minus features you rely on (LG Berlin, 67 S 150/18, Rn. 6–9). Other courts may see it differently.

staffel_index.title: Graduated rent and index rent
staffel_index.text: If you have agreed a graduated rent (Staffelmiete) or index rent (Indexmiete), an increase under § 558 BGB is excluded during this time (§ 557a Abs. 2, § 557b Abs. 2 BGB).

lwu.title: State-owned housing companies
lwu.text: At degewo, GESOBAU, Gewobag, HOWOGE, STADT UND LAND and WBM, additional voluntary commitments apply as long as the cooperation agreement (Kooperationsvereinbarung) runs (until 31.12.2027): at most 11 % more in three years (alliance agreement of 15.07.2025) and at most €50 (up to 65 m²), €75 (up to 100 m²) or €100 (up to 125 m²) more per month (Kooperationsvereinbarung II.8). There is also the affordability promise (Leistbarkeitsversprechen): on application, a net cold rent of at most 27 % of household income, if the income and floor-space limits are met.

pay_from.title: From when you would pay
pay_from.text: This is the later of the two days: the earliest day under the law or the date the landlord names. We put this date into the letter.

scope.title: Does this apply to you?
scope.text: This help only applies if your landlord asks you to consent to a higher rent (§ 558 BGB). It does not apply to an increase after modernisation (§ 559 BGB), to new advance payments for service charges (§ 560 BGB), to index or graduated rent, in social housing or another subsidised flat with a fixed rent (§ 558 Abs. 2 Satz 2 BGB), to a room in the landlord’s flat, a flat rented only for a short time or a hall of residence (§ 549 BGB). In those cases you usually have to pay the higher rent even without consent. Do not simply stop paying. Get advice.

mietpreisbremse_after_consent.title: Check the rent brake before consenting
mietpreisbremse_after_consent.text: Did your tenancy agreement start in June 2015 or later, and was the rent perhaps too high at the start? Check this before you reply. If you consent to an increase, the new rent counts as agreed. As a rule, you can then no longer rely on the rent brake (Mietpreisbremse) against this new rent (BGH, VIII ZR 300/21).

consent_deadline_193.title: Deadline for consent: next working day
consent_deadline_193.text: If your deadline ends on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Berlin, the wording of § 193 BGB puts the next working day in its place. This date shows that day. Still, plan with the earlier date. Public holidays in Berlin include, for example, New Year’s Day, Women’s Day (8 March), Good Friday, Easter Monday, 1 May, Ascension Day, Whit Monday, 3 October and the two Christmas holidays.
